sections.title: Binomial Probability Distribution
sections.content: Used for 'n' independent Bernoulli trials with probability of success 'p' and failure 'q' (p+q=1). The probability of exactly 'r' successes is P(X=r) = nCr * p^r * q^(n-r).

sections.title: Mean and Variance of Binomial Distribution
sections.content: For a binomial distribution B(n, p): Mean (Expected value E(X)) = np. Variance (Var(X)) = npq. Since q < 1, the Mean is ALWAYS strictly greater than the Variance in a binomial distribution (np > npq).

sections.title: Combined Mean and Variance
sections.content: For two groups with sizes n1, n2, means x1, x2, and variances v1, v2: Combined Mean = (n1x1 + n2x2)/(n1+n2). Combined Variance uses the formula involving deviations from the combined mean: d1 = x1 - combined_mean, d2 = x2 - combined_mean.

sections.title: Derangements in Probability
sections.content: Probability that NO item goes into its correct position (e.g., letters in envelopes). Number of derangements D(n) = n![1 - 1/1! + 1/2! - 1/3! ... + (-1)^n/n!]. P(Derangement) = D(n) / n!.

sections.title: Advanced Logical Boolean Algebra
sections.content: Treat logic statements as sets. p ∧ q is Intersection (∩). p ∨ q is Union (∪). ~p is Complement (p'). p → q is a subset (p ⊂ q). A Tautology is the Universal Set (U), and a Fallacy is the Null Set (Φ).

sections.title: Probability of Exactly One Event
sections.content: For events A and B, the probability that EXACTLY ONE occurs is P(A ∪ B) - P(A ∩ B) = P(A) + P(B) - 2P(A ∩ B). This is equivalent to symmetric difference in sets.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Assuming Variance > Mean in a Binomial Distribution (it's biologically impossible since q < 1).
2) Forgetting the 2*P(A ∩ B) subtraction when asked for 'Exactly One' event.
3) Attempting to solve complex 3-variable logic expressions with truth tables (which take 8 rows) instead of Boolean algebra rules.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 targets advanced structural probability (Binomial, Derangements), merging statistics of multiple groups (Combined Variance), and bypassing long logic truth tables using Boolean algebra/Set theory.

tricks.title: Binomial Trials Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If a problem gives Mean and Variance of a Binomial distribution, you can instantly find p, q, and n. Since Mean = np and Var = npq, divide Variance by Mean to immediately get 'q'.

tricks.title: Set Theory Logic Trick
tricks.explanation: Convert complex logic statements to set theory to solve in seconds. p ∧ (~p ∨ q) becomes A ∩ (A' ∪ B). Using distributive law: (A ∩ A') ∪ (A ∩ B) = Φ ∪ (A ∩ B) = A ∩ B = p ∧ q.
tricks.example: Saves drawing an 8-row truth table for 3 variables.

tricks.title: Negation of Bi-conditional
tricks.explanation: The negation of a bi-conditional (p ↔ q) is exactly equivalent to negating JUST ONE of the components. So, ~(p ↔ q) = (~p) ↔ q = p ↔ (~q).

tricks.title: Inclusion-Exclusion Principle (3 Events)
tricks.explanation: P(A ∪ B ∪ C) = Sum of individuals - Sum of pairs + Intersection of all three. Memorize the alternating signs (+ - +).
tricks.example: P(A) + P(B) + P(C) - P(A∩B) - P(B∩C) - P(C∩A) + P(A∩B∩C).

tricks.title: Expected Value Shortcut (E(X))
tricks.explanation: The expected value E(X) is just the Mean. E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b. For variance, Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). E(X²) is found using Var(X) = E(X²) - [E(X)]².

tricks.title: Probability of Even/Odd Successes
tricks.explanation: In a binomial distribution (q+p)^n, the probability of getting an EVEN number of successes is [1 + (q-p)^n] / 2. For an ODD number of successes, it is [1 - (q-p)^n] / 2.
tricks.example: Instantly sums alternate terms in binomial expansions.
